## Synopsis

```text
perch mail send [OPTIONS]
```

## Description

Compose a MIME message and submit it through SMTP. Text and HTML bodies are combined as multipart/alternative; attachments wrap the result in multipart/mixed.

Bodies come from --body/--body-file and --html-body/--html-file, or stdin when it is not a terminal. Attachments are base64 encoded and content types are detected from the file extension or contents.

## Notes

- Bodies are quoted-printable unless --8bitmime is set; attachments are base64.
- SMTPUTF8 is detected from non-ASCII envelope addresses and extra headers; force it with --smtputf8.
- Bcc recipients are envelope-only and never appear in headers.
- SIZE is sent automatically and checked against the server's advertised limit.

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--username, -u <value>` | account username (env PERCH_IMAP_USER) |
| `--password <value>` | account password (prefer PERCH_IMAP_PASSWORD or --password-file) |
| `--password-file <value>` | read the account password from a file |
| `--password-stdin` | read the account password from stdin |
| `--timeout <value>` | connection timeout (default: 30s) |
| `--config <value>` | configuration file (default: ~/.config/perch/perch.yaml) |
| `--from <value>` | sender address (default: --username) |
| `--to <value>...` | recipient address or list; repeatable |
| `--cc <value>...` | Cc recipient address or list; repeatable |
| `--bcc <value>...` | Bcc recipient address or list; repeatable |
| `--reply-to <value>...` | Reply-To address or list; repeatable |
| `--subject, -s <value>` | message subject |
| `--body <value>` | plain-text body |
| `--body-file <value>` | read the plain-text body from a file (use - for stdin) |
| `--html-body <value>` | HTML body |
| `--html-file <value>` | read the HTML body from a file (use - for stdin) |
| `--attach, -a <value>...` | attach a file; repeatable |
| `--header, -H <value>...` | add an extra header (Name: Value); repeatable |
| `--in-reply-to <value>` | Message-ID being replied to |
| `--references <value>` | space-separated Message-IDs for References |
| `--8bitmime` | send UTF-8 text with BODY=8BITMIME |
| `--smtputf8` | force SMTPUTF8 (usually detected automatically) |
| `--dry-run, -n` | write the composed message to stdout without sending |
| `--verbose, -v` | print SMTP capabilities and delivery details to stderr |
| `--smtp-server, -S <value>` | SMTP submission server (smtps://host, smtp://host, or host[:port]); defaults from --config |
| `--smtp-plaintext` | connect to SMTP without TLS (use only on trusted networks) |
| `--smtp-starttls` | require STARTTLS for SMTP |
| `--smtp-implicit-tls` | use implicit TLS for SMTP (usually port 465) |
| `--smtp-insecure` | skip SMTP TLS certificate verification |
| `--smtp-ca-file <value>` | PEM CA bundle used to verify the SMTP server certificate |
| `--help, -h` | show help |

## Examples

```sh
perch mail send --from you@example.com --to alice@example.com \
  --subject Hello --body 'Hi Alice'

echo 'Body from stdin' | perch mail send --from you@example.com \
  --to alice@example.com --subject Hello

perch mail send --from you@example.com --to alice@example.com \
  --subject Report --body-file message.txt --html-file message.html \
  --attach report.pdf

perch mail send ... --dry-run > message.eml
```

## Environment

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PERCH_IMAP_USER` | default account username and sender |
| `PERCH_IMAP_PASSWORD` | account password |
